claims.text_en: Khet Bangkok Noi (บางกอกน้อย, geocode 1071) is a west-bank khet of 11.944 km2 with five khwaeng: Siri Rat 1.258 km2, Ban Chang Lo 2.076, Bang Khun Non 1.492, Bang Khun Si 4.360 (largest), Arun Amarin 2.758; English Wikipedia's table gives 112,046 residents at 2017 (app's 103,791 is a later vintage). Established as Amphoe Ammarin 15 Oct 1915, renamed Bangkok Noi 11 Jul 1916, became a khet in the 1972 merger, lost Bang Phlat on 9 Nov 1989, and gained its current khwaeng set when Arun Amarin was created on 12 Dec 1991. OSM relations: khet 2942282, khwaeng relations 11355120-24.

evidence.paraphrase: area, five khwaeng with areas, 1915/1916/1972/1989/1991 dates

limitations: 2017 population vintage differs from app value

claims.text_en: Siriraj Hospital - Thailand's first western hospital, with its medical/forensic museums - sits by the mouth of Khlong Bangkok Noi in khwaeng Siri Rat (verified, per the brief's tension item). Beside it stands the 1903 Bangkok Noi railway terminus (Karl Doehring's Brick Expressionism building, renamed Thon Buri in 1942, WWII Japanese base for Burma Railway supply, closed to trains 4 Oct 2003), reopened in 2013 as the Siriraj Bimuksthan Museum.

evidence.paraphrase: first western hospital; near Khlong Bangkok Noi mouth; medical museum
opened 19 Jun 1903; renamed Thonburi 1942; trains last served 3 Oct 2003; museum from 2013; khwaeng Siri Rat

claims.text_en: The railway-village tension resolved: the operational terminus is Thon Buri station (สถานีธนบุรี) on Rotfai Road, khwaeng Siriraj - 'Terminus for ordinary and commuter trains', a class-1 station renamed from Bangkok Noi on 1 Jan 2004, next stop Charansanitwong Halt toward Taling Chan, and the Southern Line's kilometre 0 is still measured from it (EN Wikipedia). Seat 61 confirms current service: the two daily local trains to Kanchanaburi and Nam Tok depart from Thonburi, which is a stated 9-minute/750 m walk from MRT Bang Khun Non; long-distance services moved instead to Krung Thep Aphiwat on 19 Jan 2023. The SRT corridor still runs through the khet (Charansanitwong and Bang Ramat halts nearby).

evidence.paraphrase: terminus for ordinary and commuter trains; class 1; renamed 1 Jan 2004; next stop Charansanitwong Halt

claims.text_en: Wang Lang Market (next to Siriraj, on Phra Nnok Road at the river) runs every day 08:00-18:00 with free entry; it is a worker-and-student food market famous for desserts and southern-Thai dishes, with almost no English signage, reached by the Chao Phraya express boat to Prannok (N10) or Wang Lang pier ferries to Tha Phra Chan and Tha Chang (Your Thai Guide; EN Wikipedia lists Wang Lang among khet markets with the piers). This is the concrete face of food 7.

claims.text_en: Heritage and rhythm: the khet's older layer is canal-first - the district grew around Khlong Bangkok Noi (the Chao Phraya's former main channel), with the Royal Barges National Museum on the northern rim, Wat Suwannaram (a former royal cremation site that also hosted the old district office) and riverside Wat Rakhang on the other rim (EN Wikipedia). The weekly rhythm is set by the hospital economy (Siriraj staff and students feed Wang Lang daily) and the twice-daily Kanchanaburi local trains (seat 61; EN wiki services box) - a working district, not a leisure district.

evidence.paraphrase: Khlong Bangkok Noi as historic channel; Royal Barges Museum; Wat Suwannaram; Wat Rakhang

question_answers.notes: Khet Bangkok Noi, 11.944 km2, 5 khwaeng (Siri Rat 1.258 / Ban Chang Lo 2.076 / Bang Khun Non 1.492 / Bang Khun Si 4.360 / Arun Amarin 2.758). In: Siriraj Hospital (khwaeng Siri Rat - verified), old Bangkok Noi station = Siriraj Bimuksthan Museum, operational Thon Buri terminus (khwaeng Siriraj), Wang Lang market, Central Pinklao, MRT Fai Chai + Bang Khun Non, piers N10/N11.

Three daily lives: the Siriraj river corner (hospital workers, Wang Lang 8-18 daily), the Charan/Fai Chai condo corridor, and inland Bang Khun Si (bus/SRT-halt life). Inland texture thin in sources read.

Transport 7: two MRT Blue stations + express-boat piers + functioning Thonburi terminus (two daily Kanchanaburi/Nam Tok locals; 750 m from Bang Khun Non MRT). Long-distance trains left for Krung Thep Aphiwat (19 Jan 2023), so the terminus is a commuter/heritage stop, not a regional gateway.

Counter-view: amenity density collapses away from the river/MRT corner - largest khwaeng (Bang Khun Si) holds neither MRT station nor named mall in the data read; transport 7 (not higher) and DE 8 (mall+markets) both defensible but spatially uneven.

Rhythm: hospital workdays feed Wang Lang 08:00-18:00; two daily Kanchanaburi locals (07:45 out per TrueID listing, snippet-flagged); express boats all day; temple calendar around Wat Suwannaram/Wat Rakhang unsourced.

Walkability prose absent; sourced adjacency: Thonburi station 750 m from MRT Bang Khun Non (seat61 statement, not a radius conversion); Wang Lang starts at the pier. Riverside lanes and market sois imply fine-grained walking, unsourced.
Daily life: Central Pinklao mall + four named markets (Wang Lang, Pran Nok, Bang Khun Si, Chaitit); hospital economy; boat commutes.
Rent 9 / 12,000-25,000: HipFlat 292 listings, 1BR USD443 avg, sample asks 11k-23k THB on the Charan corridor - editorial band fits comfortably.

Green 7 on 0.8% park share reads river-and-khlong-based: several named small parks (OSM) incl. Rama IX royal garden and Suan Bang Khun Non; no large park; promenade character unsourced but consistent.
Fits: medical students/workers (Siriraj), heritage walkers, value renters on the Charan corridor. Poor fit: park-heavy family life, metro-first commuters living inland (Bang Khun Si).

2024-2026: the consequential change is systemic - long-distance rail consolidation at Krung Thep Aphiwat since 19 Jan 2023 leaves Thonburi as local/commuter terminus; no khet-specific 2024-2026 event found in queries run.
Outside-the-score: halts' khwaeng membership unresolved; per-park areas unmeasured; nightlife-46 composition unknown (no source read); Siriraj-driven parking/street pressure unquantified.

preview.text_en: A hospital-and-railway district on the river: Siriraj anchors the bank, Wang Lang market feeds it daily, and the twice-daily Kanchanaburi local still steams out of Thonburi station - cheap Charan-corridor rents between.

guide_lead.text_en: Bangkok Noi is the west bank at its most working: Thailand's first western hospital, Siriraj, owns the riverfront, the old 1903 Bangkok Noi terminus survives as the Siriraj Bimuksthan museum, and the operating Thonburi station still sends two local trains a day toward Kanchanaburi - a 750-metre walk from the MRT. Wang Lang market runs daily at the pier; Central Pinklao anchors the retail. Two Blue Line stations (Fai Chai, Bang Khun Non) plus boat piers carry the commute. Rents track the Charan Sanitwong corridor (about 11k-23k in listed 2026 stock). The honest trade-offs: the green is riverside-and-temple rather than parkland, and convenience thins quickly inland.

strengths.text_en: A rare working heritage-rail link: Thonburi station (khwaeng Siriraj) still runs the daily Kanchanaburi/Nam Tok locals, 750 m from MRT Bang Khun Non - verified in two independent rail sources.
Food economy with a real anchor: Wang Lang market's daily 08:00-18:00 worker trade at the Siriraj pier, plus Pran Nok, Bang Khun Si and Chaitit markets and Central Pinklao for everything else.

tradeoffs.text_en: Conveniences cluster on the river/MRT corner: largest khwaeng Bang Khun Si holds no MRT station in the data read - inland daily life leans on buses and SRT halts.
Park share is 0.8% (9.4 ha); green means the riverbank, khlong rims and temple grounds rather than a destination park.

day_night.text_en: Days run on Siriraj's clock - Wang Lang fills 08:00-18:00 with hospital and student trade; nights quiet down fast on the khwaeng lanes, with the Charan strip and Central Pinklao carrying the late errands.

within_area_variation.text_en: The Siriraj/Wang Lang river corner (khwaeng Siri Rat) is dense with institutions and food; the Charan/Fai Chai corridor (Ban Chang Lo side) is the condo belt; Bang Khun Si inland is the quietest and least rail-served corner.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit for medical/students tied to Siriraj and for renters who want 1BRs around 11-16k with MRT-plus-boat commutes.
Weak fit if you need park-rich weekends or evening scenes - nightlife count is modest (46) and the big green is the river itself.

editorial.uncertainties: No body-read source describes nightlife composition or street walkability; hours/prices at Wang Lang are blog-sourced and could drift; park areas per OSM ways unmeasured; TrueID timetable (07:45 train 257) is snippet-level only; population vintages differ (2017 EN wiki vs app).

open_issues: Confirm by app polygon which khwaeng the Charansanitwong and Bang Ramat SRT halts fall in (khet Bangkok Noi vs Bang Phlat) - matters for transport-crediting on the corridor.
